basis: Dictated canon only (ADR 0018): TBWTT Yahweh paragraphs and ETTMTTP chapter 2 Yahweh paragraphs. LWTE and ETTMTTP chapter 3 are author opinion and ground no entry. Quotes are verbatim from data-library (EN i18n.en, FR text).

rules.selection: An entry exists only where a dictated paragraph states what the Genesis term is. Where the canon decodes partly (paraphrase, or a gloss not attached to the quoted verse) the entry is labelled inferred and flagged in notes.
applicationOrder: the remaining entries in any order
rules.agreement: After a swap, fix pronoun and verb agreement in the same sentence only (he->they etc. where the antecedent is the decoded term). Antecedents need a human check: verses with Elohim/YHWH plus he/his/him: 1:3-1:31 (passim), 2:2-2:22, 3:1-3:23, 4:1-4:26, 5:1, 5:22-29, 6:3-6:22, 7:1-7:16, 8:1-8:21, 9:1-9:27, 10:9, 11:6-11:9.
rules.noMarking: Founder ruling 2026-11-28: swapped words carry no visual marking in the Reading.

variants.the Elohim / The Elohim: the Sky People / The Sky People
variants.agreement: Plural agreement: narrative he/his/him/himself whose antecedent is the Elohim -> they/their/them/themselves; singular verbs -> plural (3:1 'Has the Elohim really said' -> 'Have the Sky People really said'; 3:3 'has said' -> 'have said'; 3:5 'knows' -> 'know'; 4:25 'has appointed' -> 'have appointed'). First-person singular inside direct speech stays as printed pending openQuestions Q2.

scope.applies: Every occurrence in Gen 1-11 (53x 'the Elohim' incl. sentence-initial, plus bare 5:1 and 9:26). Not applied inside 'YHWH-Elohim' (entry yhwh takes precedence) or inside 'sons of the Elohim' (entry benei-ha-elohim takes precedence).
scope.exceptions: None in Gen 1-11: every Elohim there denotes the creators. For the later Genesis lenses the literal sense must stay where elohim means household or foreign gods: 31:30, 31:32 ('my elohim', 'your elohim', Laban's teraphim), 35:2, 35:4 ('the foreign elohim'); layer 2 prints these lower-case.

quote.en: Elohim, unjustly translated in some Bibles as God, means in Hebrew “those who came from the sky,” and it is indeed in the plural. This means that the scientists from our world first sought the planet that seemed to them most suitable for carrying out their projects.
quote.fr: Elohim, injustement traduit dans certaines Bibles par Dieu, veut dire en Hébreu «ceux qui sont venus du ciel» et est bel et bien au pluriel. Cela veut dire que les scientifiques issus de notre monde ont d’abord recherché la planète leur paraissant la plus apte à la réalisation de leurs projets.

quote.en: If you want to give us a name, although we call ourselves men in our language, you can call us «Elohim», since we have «come from the sky».
quote.fr: Si vous voulez nous donner un nom, bien que nous nous appelions des hommes dans notre langue, vous pouvez nous appeler des «Elohim» puisque nous sommes «venus du ciel».

entries.notes: Founder ruling 2026-11-28: decoded Reading = 'the Sky People'; the Meaning lens uses 'those who came from the sky' at first mention per chapter, then 'the Sky People'. The canon's gloss is a canonical rendering, not the consensus lexical derivation (claim 0009 records this). TBWTT-3:251 repeats the gloss ("Elohim, that means literally «those come from the sky» in Hebrew"). At 3:5 TBWTT-2:34 prints 'ye shall be as gods' but TBWTT-2:35 decodes it as being 'as strong as their creators', so 'like the Sky People' is canon-backed.

quote.en: The exiled creators, who remained under military surveillance, urged the men to bring them food in order to show their superiors that the beings they had created were good and would never turn against their fathers.
quote.fr: Les créateurs exilés, qui restaient sous surveillance militaire, poussèrent les hommes à leur amener de la nourriture afin de montrer à leurs supérieurs que les êtres qu’ils avaient créés étaient bons et ne se retourneraient jamais contre leurs pères.

quote.en: The creators were happy to see that the men wished them well, and promised never to try to destroy them in the future, for they had understood that it was normal for them to want to make progress.
quote.fr: Les créateurs furent heureux de voir que les hommes leur voulaient du bien et promirent de ne jamais essayer de les détruire à l’avenir, car ils avaient compris qu’il était normal qu’ils veuillent faire des progrès.

quote.en: The “serpent”—that small group of creators who had wanted to teach Adam and Eve the truth—was condemned by the government of the original planet to live on Earth in exile, while the other creators had to stop their experiments and leave the Earth.
quote.fr: Le «serpent», ce petit groupe de créateurs qui avait voulu apprendre la vérité à Adam et Ève, était condamné par le gouvernement de la planète originelle à vivre sur Terre en exil tandis que les autres créateurs devaient stopper leurs expériences et quitter la Terre.

quote.en: I myself directed the creation of life on the Earth.
quote.fr: J’ai moi-même dirigé la création de la vie sur la Terre.

quote.en: My name is Yahweh and I am the president of the council of the eternals.
quote.fr: Mon nom est Iahvé et je suis le président du conseil des éternels.

entries.notes: PARTIAL DECODING, flagged. The canon never glosses the name YHWH inside Genesis. Every time it quotes a Genesis YHWH verse it paraphrases the actor as the creators: 4:3-4 'unto Yahweh' -> 'the exiled creators' (2:47-48); 8:20 'unto Yahweh' -> 'The creators were happy' (2:65-66); 6:5 'Yahweh saw' -> 'Good, for them' (2:56-57); 11:8 'Yahweh scattered them' -> 'They came' = the people of the planet (2:74-76); 3:14 'Yahweh Elohim said unto the serpent' -> condemned 'by the government of the original planet' while 'the other creators had to stop their experiments' (2:38-39). So for those five verses 'the creators' is framework; extending it to all 50 occurrences is inferred. Separately the canon names Yahweh as an individual, the president of the Council of the Eternals, who 'directed the creation of life on the Earth' (TBWTT-7:56; ETTMTTP-2:50; claim 0028), but it never attributes a Genesis YHWH act to that individual; the individual reading of 3:14 appears only in LWTE-2:24 (author opinion, cannot ground). Note the canon's referent shifts (government, majority, exiles), which the collective 'the creators' covers and an individual name would not. Matches the earlier founder ruling (2026-11-27/28: YHWH and YHWH-Elohim = 'the creators' in lenses 3-4). See openQuestions Q1.

quote.en: These studies took a fair amount of time. The “day” corresponds to the period during which your sun rises under the same sign on the day of the spring equinox—that is, about two thousand Earth years.
quote.fr: Ces études prirent pas mal de temps. Le «jour» correspond à la période pendant laquelle votre soleil se lève sous le même signe le jour de l’équinoxe de printemps, soit deux mille ans terrestres environ.

entries.notes: The canon decodes the unit explicitly: a 'day' is the span in which the sun rises under one sign at the spring equinox, 'about two thousand Earth years', i.e. one precessional age. Number caution (canon-map): the canon figure is ~2,000 years; claim 0059's ~2,160 is the corpus lattice, label it framework and cite the canon figure first. 'evening' and 'morning' stay literal (the canon does not decode them). 'age' avoids the site's banned 'astrological ages'. See openQuestions Q3.

samples.after: The deluge was on the land forty days; the waters increased and lifted up the rocket, and it rose above the land.

scope.exceptions: Proposed literal in the narrative of boarding, where a swap breaks the sentence ('they came to Noah ... two by two'): 7:2-3 'seven pairs', 7:8-9, 7:14-16 (Q7).

quote.en: containing a couple of each species to be safeguarded. This is an image. In reality—and your scientific knowledge will soon allow you to understand it—it is enough to have a living cell of each species, male and female, to then reconstitute the whole being.
quote.fr: contenant un couple de chaque espèce à sauvegarder. Ceci est une image. En réalité, et vos connaissances scientifiques vous permettront bientôt de le comprendre, il suffit d’avoir une cellule vivante de chaque espèce, mâle et femelle, pour reconstituer ensuite l’être tout entier.

entries.notes: The canon says outright that the pairs are 'an image' for cells. 'male and female' stays, as in the canon's own wording.

samples.before: Of every living thing, of all flesh, two of each you shall bring into the ark to keep alive with you — male and female they shall be.
samples.after: Of every living thing, of all flesh, a living cell of each you shall bring into the rocket to keep alive with you — male and female they shall be.

samples.before: Of the birds according to their kind, and of the cattle according to their kind, and of every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind — two of each shall come to you, to be kept alive.
samples.after: Of the birds according to their kind, and of the cattle according to their kind, and of every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind — a living cell of each shall come to you, to be kept alive.

variants.was only evil (6:5): was only the desire to progress
variants.is evil from his youth (8:21): is the desire to progress from his youth

scope.exceptions: 6:5 'the wickedness of the human' (ra'at, FR quote 'malice') stays literal (Q8). 'good and bad' in 2:9, 2:17, 3:5, 3:22 stays literal (2:9/2:17 are absorbed by the etz-ha-daat entry). 6:11-13 'corrupted', 'violence' stay literal (canon silent).

quote.en: Evil—that is, the desire to become a people equal to its creators, a scientific and independent people. Good, for them, was that man should remain a primitive being vegetating on Earth. Evil was that he should want to make progress, risking one day being in a position to rejoin his creators.
quote.fr: Le mal, c’est-à-dire le désir de devenir un peuple égal à ses créateurs, un peuple scientifique et indépendant. Le bien pour eux était que l’homme demeure un être primitif végétant sur la Terre. Le mal était qu’il veuille faire des progrès, risquant un jour d’être en mesure de rejoindre ses créateurs.

quote.en: Man’s goal is scientific progress.
quote.fr: Le but de l’homme est le progrès scientifique.

entries.notes: TBWTT-2:56 quotes 6:5 and 2:57 decodes 'evil' as the creators' word for humanity's wish to progress; TBWTT-2:67 quotes 8:21 ('the imagination of man's heart is evil') and 2:68 answers 'Man's goal is scientific progress'. Longer canon-exact alternative: 'the desire to equal the creators'.

samples.before: YHWH saw that the wickedness of the human was great on the land, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all day long.
samples.after: The creators saw that the wickedness of the human was great on the land, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only the desire to progress all day long.

samples.before: YHWH smelled the soothing aroma, and YHWH said in his heart, "I will not again curse the ground because of the human, for the inclination of the heart of the human is evil from his youth; and I will not again strike down every living thing as I have done.
samples.after: The creators smelled the soothing aroma, and the creators said in their heart, "I will not again curse the ground because of the human, for the inclination of the heart of the human is the desire to progress from his youth; and I will not again strike down every living thing as I have done.

scope.exceptions: 'city' stays literal (the canon does not decode it); 'Babel' (11:9) stays a name.

quote.en: So they built an immense rocket: the Tower of Babel.
quote.fr: Ils construisirent donc une immense fusée : la Tour de Babel.

entries.notes: TBWTT-2:72 is commentary placed before its quote of 11:6 (2:73); the equation is explicit. 'with its top in the skies' stays literal and now reads naturally.

scope.applies: 1:21: no swap; layer 2's "the great dragons" is kept (founder accepted Q11 A).

quote.en: Dragons, or what you have named Dinosaurs or Brontosaurs, and so on.
quote.fr: Des dragons ou ce que vous avez baptisé des Dinosaures ou autres Brontosaures, etc.

entries.notes: Founder ruling 2026-11-28 (Q11 A): keep "the great dragons", the canon's own word. Dinosaur gloss, not used in the Reading: TBWTT-2:22 decodes its own word "dragons" as dinosaurs ("Dragons, or what you have named Dinosaurs or Brontosaurs"), in commentary on the day-5 stage, but it does not quote Gen 1:21 (it passes from 1:20 at 2:19 to 1:24 at 2:23). Linking that gloss to tanninim is the corpus's reading (claim 0073, public label speculative), so "the great dinosaurs" would be inferred at best. The Meaning lens may cite the canon's gloss. Layer 2 already prints 'great dragons'.

samples.before: And the Elohim shaped the great dragons, and every living being that moves, with which the waters swarmed, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And the Elohim saw that it was good.
samples.after: And the Elohim shaped the great dragons, and every living being that moves, with which the waters swarmed, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And the Elohim saw that it was good.

rejected.term: ruach Elohim (1:2) 'the breath of the Elohim hovering'
rejected.reason: TBWTT-2:6 quotes the line and 2:7 describes reconnaissance trips and 'what you might call artificial satellites', but never says what the ruach is. Scene-level commentary, not a gloss. Only 'Elohim' inside it is swapped ('the breath of the Sky People').
The canon decodes the waters above (clouds) and below (ocean), not the dome; in 1:14-20 the dome is simply the sky. Claim 0039 treats the firmament as the account's observational vocabulary.
TBWTT-2:7 confirms the literal picture ('entirely covered with water and thick mists'); no gloss of tehom.
TBWTT-2:16 reinterprets the act (plant cells made from chemicals in a laboratory) but keeps the plants as plants. Nothing to swap.

TBWTT-2:18 reinterprets the act as observation of the sun and stars for measuring time; the lights are literally the sun and stars, which layer 2 already says. Verb-level reinterpretation, not a term decoding.
The canon confirms the literal sense: 'In our image! You can see that the resemblance is striking' (TBWTT-2:27; also 5:62). Keep.
The canon calls him 'a man' made artificially; no gloss of the word.
TBWTT-2:28 identifies the garden as the team's territory ('what you call the earthly paradise'), which leaves the word 'garden' accurate. Only 3:23-24 is decoded (entry gan-eden-residence).
TBWTT-2:41 says 'The Bible has here preserved a phrase almost intact from the original document': literal by the canon's own word.
Already literal; the 'us' resolves once the speaker is decoded. TBWTT-2:43 explains the equality ('our equals'), it does not replace the words.
TBWTT-2:37 ('they understood that they too could become creators') decodes the sentence, not a term. Belongs in the Meaning lens.

rejected.term: the curse on the serpent: 'on your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat' (3:14)
rejected.reason: TBWTT-2:39 gives the sentence's meaning (exile on Earth). Sentence-level; Meaning lens.
The canon omits the Nephilim clause from its quote of 6:4 (TBWTT-2:54). The Watchers/Nephilim identification is the corpus's (claim 0012, comparative).

rejected.term: gibborim 'the mighty ones ... men of name' (6:4)
rejected.reason: TBWTT-2:55 says the unions gave 'exceptional children'; this restates who they were (the verse already says they were the offspring) rather than decoding the word.

rejected.term: 'My breath shall not abide in the human forever' (6:3)
rejected.reason: TBWTT-2:53 explains the consequence (longevity not hereditary; the tree of life not inherited) without glossing ruach. Meaning lens.
The canon keeps the waters real ('The continent was submerged by an immense tidal wave', TBWTT-2:58); it decodes the cause (nuclear missiles), which the word does not name. Keep 'deluge'.

rejected.reason: TBWTT-2:64 and 2:60 reinterpret the period (removing radioactivity, waiting out fallout) without glossing the words.
Quoted at TBWTT-2:65 without a gloss; 2:64's 'share ... for their subsistence' is supportive, not an equation (Q9).

Canon comments only by allusion (2:64, 2:66); 9:4-5 has only LWTE-1:69 (author opinion).
TBWTT-2:76 ('They came ... scattered them ... in countries where none could make himself understood') confirms the literal descent and explains the confusion as dispersal; nothing to swap.

openQuestions.question: How should the decoded Reading render YHWH and YHWH-Elohim now that Elohim is 'the Sky People'?
options: A (recommended): 'the creators' for both, as ruled 2026-11-27/28. It is the canon's own paraphrase in all five Genesis YHWH verses it decodes (3:14, 4:3-4, 6:5, 8:20, 11:8), and it keeps the Hebrew name shift visible: Gen 1 'the Sky People', Gen 2-11 'the creators'.

B: 'Yahweh' (the Council president, claim 0028) for YHWH, 'Yahweh of the Sky People' for YHWH-Elohim. The canon never assigns a Genesis act to the individual; at 3:14 it names the government, at 11:8 'the people of the planet'.
C: 'the Sky People' for all three names. Simplest, but erases the name shift and is not the canon's wording for these verses.

openQuestions.question: Divine direct speech after a plural subject: 'The Sky People said to Noah, "... I am about to destroy them"' (6:13, 6:17, 9:9-17; also YHWH speech in 6:7, 7:1-4, 8:21).
options: A (recommended): keep 'I/me/my' as printed: one speaks for the group, and the Hebrew is singular.
B: switch to 'we/us/our' throughout direct speech.

openQuestions.question: Creation 'day' in the Reading.
options: A (recommended): 'age' ('age one', 'the sixth age'), with day 7 (2:2-3) included as an inferred extension.
B: 'period' (neutral, but loses the canon's equinox-sign definition).
C: 'age' for days 1-6 only; keep 'the seventh day' (canon silent on Gen 2:1-3).

openQuestions.question: The tree of knowing good and bad.
options: A (recommended): 'the scientific books' (TBWTT-2:30's words), named occurrences 2:9 and 2:17 only; 'eat' stays as the image TBWTT-3:169 names.
B: 'the tree of scientific knowledge' (keeps the tree image, swaps only its content).
C: A, and also decode the unnamed 'tree' in 3:3-17.

openQuestions.question: Should 'the creators' residence' replace 'the garden' beyond 3:23-24?
options: A (recommended): no. Only 3:23-24, where TBWTT-2:45 says it; the garden elsewhere is the team's territory (2:28), which 'garden' already conveys.
B: replace every 'garden (of Eden)' in Gen 2-3 (reads oddly in 2:8 'planted a residence', 2:15 'to work it').

openQuestions.question: Ark -> 'the rocket' leaves layer-2 phrases that clash with the canon: 6:14 'gopher wood ... pitch', 7:18 'the ark went on the face of the waters' (TBWTT-2:60: 'not upon the waters').
options: A (recommended): keep the shape; the Meaning lens and its note carry the canon's correction.
B: leave 'ark' in 7:18 only.

openQuestions.question: Pairs -> cells: how far?
options: A (recommended): only the instruction, 6:19-20.
B: also 7:2-3, 7:9, 7:15 (breaks 'they came to Noah ... two by two').

openQuestions.question: 'evil' (6:5, 8:21) -> 'the desire to progress': also swap 'wickedness' in 6:5?
options: A (recommended): swap 'evil' (ra) only; TBWTT-2:57 glosses 'Evil' (le mal), while the quoted 'wickedness' is ra'at ('malice').
B: swap both ('the desire to progress of the human was great').

openQuestions.question: Offerings: 4:3-5 minchah -> 'food' is canon-explicit (TBWTT-2:48). Extend to 8:20 burnt offerings?
options: A (recommended): no; keep 8:20 literal.
B: 8:20 'offered whole burnt offerings' -> 'gave a share for their subsistence' (TBWTT-2:64).

openQuestions.question: Edge verses for the YHWH/Elohim swap: 4:1 'I have made a man — YHWH himself!', 4:26 'called on the name of YHWH', 9:26 'blessed be YHWH, Elohim of Shem'.
options: A (recommended): 4:1 keep 'YHWH' (Hebrew crux, canon silent; 'the creators themselves!' misleads); 4:26 'the name of the creators'; 9:26 'blessed be the creators, the Sky People of Shem'.
B: apply mechanically everywhere, including 4:1.

openQuestions.question: Gen 1:21 tanninim: swap 'the great dragons' for 'the great dinosaurs'?
options: A (recommended): no. 'dragons' is the canon's own word; the dinosaur gloss is attached to Gen 1:21 only by claim 0073 (speculative).
B: swap, labelled inferred.

openQuestions.question: Meaning lens naming for the YHWH strand (Gen 2-11) once Elohim = 'those who came from the sky' / 'the Sky People'.
options: A (recommended): keep 'the creators' (the canon's own word in its Genesis commentary), with 'those who came from the sky' at the first Elohim mention per chapter.
B: use 'the Sky People' for both strands in the Meaning lens.

openQuestions.question: The serpent: 'the small group of creators' (TBWTT-2:39) produces 3:14 'The creators said to the small group of creators' and keeps 3:1's comparison with wild animals.
options: A (recommended): accept: it is the canon's contrast (the condemned group vs. the government and the other creators).
B: a shorter label such as 'the small group' after first mention in the chapter.

founderRulings: creation days 1:5–2:3 = 'age one … the seventh age' (seventh inferred)
ark = 'the rocket', words swapped only, Meaning note corrects clashing sentences
all remaining recommended handling accepted (open questions resolved as recommended)
